newsitem.title: USA: S&P says not ready to raise DC "junk" bond rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P says not ready to raise DC "junk" bond rating.

text.p: The financially ailing District of Columbia has made some progress under the supervision of its financial control board, but much more work is needed before Standard & Poor's Corp. will raise the city's "junk" rating, S&P said on Monday.
S&P said in its weekly credit report that the city is paying more attention to improving the financial systems that track city operations. And D.C. has set up procedures to better control spending.
But the District still suffers from a deep-rooted budget imbalance, S&P said.

"This chronic imbalance, combined with a stagnant economy, escalating Medicaid costs, high debt ...., and a large unfunded pension liability, continue to keep the District's long-term bond rating (at a) noninvestment grade," S&P said.

S&P said the control board's "strategic plan" for the city issued late in 1996 is a step in the right direction because it highlights major District problems and begins to set timetables to remedy them."
This and a D.C. financial rescue package proposed by the Clinton Administration recently "have the potential to improve the Disrict's financial health," S&P said.
"However, significant progress toward successful implememtation of these ideas will be required before any positive rating action is taken," S&P said.
S&P's rating for D.C.'s general obligation bonds is 'B' with a stable outlook.
